excerpt: Virta Health is a US virtual clinic that treats type 2 diabetes and obesity with a nutrition-first approach, paid for mainly by employers and health plans. Valued at $2B after a $133M Series E in 2021.
content:
Virta Health is a virtual medical clinic in the United States that treats type 2 diabetes, prediabetes and obesity. Its approach is nutrition-first: members get a personalised eating plan, remote monitoring, coaching and medical supervision through an app, and a medical team adjusts diabetes medication as their numbers change. Virta says it works with or without GLP-1 drugs and describes its mission as reversing metabolic disease in one billion people.

Virta's leadership page names Sami Inkinen as co-founder and chief executive, with Stephen Phinney, MD, PhD (former chief medical officer) and Jeff Volek, PhD (former chief science officer) as the other co-founders.

Most members get Virta through an employer or health plan. Its FAQ says there is no fee to apply, that people covered through an employer-sponsored health plan pay no treatment cost, and that others may qualify for up to a 60% discount based on household size and income.

In April 2021 Virta raised $133 million in a Series E led by Tiger Global, which Fierce Biotech reported valued the company at $2 billion. That came a few months after a $65 million Series D in December 2020. The company said the money would fund research, product development and demand from employers, health plans and government buyers. Outcome figures Virta publishes come from its own research.

This profile is drawn from Virta's own pages and published reporting. It is not medical advice. We have not used the service, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.summary_short: Virtual clinic for type 2 diabetes and weight loss using a nutrition-first approach

fit: live in the US with type 2 diabetes, prediabetes or obesity
get health cover through an employer or plan that partners with Virta
want a diet-led approach with a medical team watching your medication
not_fit: do not want to change your diet substantially; the programme is nutrition-first

pricing.intro: Virta does not publish a list price. Its FAQ says there is no fee to apply, that people covered through an employer-sponsored health plan pay no treatment cost, and that others may qualify for up to a 60% discount off the annual cost based on household size and income.

plans.name: Through an employer or health plan
plans.detail: Per Virta's FAQ, for people covered by a partnering employer-sponsored plan

plans.name: Self-pay
plans.detail: Income-based discounts of up to 60% may apply

notes: Check eligibility on Virta's site; coverage depends on your employer or plan.

pros: Often free to members through their employer or health plan
Medical supervision for reducing diabetes medication

alternatives.intro: Other virtual programmes for diabetes and weight. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: Omada Health
items.what: Virtual care for diabetes, prediabetes, hypertension and weight
items.difference: Broader chronic-condition programme, also sold mainly through employers and plans.

items.name: Livongo (Teladoc Health)
items.what: Connected glucose meter and coaching for diabetes
items.difference: Centres on remote glucose monitoring rather than a diet-led reversal plan.

items.name: Noom
items.difference: Consumer self-pay app focused on weight and behaviour change.
